## Texts and drawings (6)

- **E0920** (poem, sure): 招凉榭. 嘉庆十八年 (1813) · v4 p.319, under 含辉楼; source ref 5-271 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=322
  > 楼南射圃绿阴长，虚榭空明竹榻凉。碧毯遥连桥略彴，鸣蝉嘒嘒树千章。沼澄林静景清寥，坐挹凉飔不待招。翠盖亭亭擎凈植，欣看君子具丰标。
  Poem 招凉榭 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1813, filed by the editors under 含辉楼.
- **E0921** (poem, sure): 招凉榭. 嘉庆二十一年 (1816) · v4 p.320, under 含辉楼; source ref 6-213 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=323
  > 楼西地高敞，虚榭临陂塘。簷楹遍通达，木榻依砌长。四面来爽籁，雨足气候凉。密荫铺岸柳，碧线薰风扬。坐观庶汇茂，弥觉农务忙。心惬肃乂顺，治协由年康。
  Poem 招凉榭 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1816, filed by the editors under 含辉楼.
- **E0922** (poem, sure): 招凉榭. 嘉庆二十五年 (1820) · v4 p.321, under 含辉楼; source ref 7-324 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=324
  > 菜畦花圃绕楼前，虚榭空明爽气延。东沼荷香遥岸送，西山林影远村连。润含心境一瓯茗，静悟闻思众木蝉。序入新秋消伏暑，生生不息四时旋。
  Poem 招凉榭 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1820, filed by the editors under 含辉楼.
- **E0923** (poem, likely): 招凉榭观荷（72）. 咸丰八年 (1858) · v4 p.323, under 含辉楼 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=326
  > 虚榭楼南绿影长，森森夏木印方塘。锦云翠盖标清兴，盈沼芙蕖一槛香。
  Poem 招凉榭观荷（72） by the Xianfeng Emperor, 1858, filed by the editors under 含辉楼.
- **E0506** (description, sure): 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 绮春园. 2020 edition · v4 p.170 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=173
  Formed from princes' and ministers' gardens, about 54.3 ha. Taken back from Fuheng's heirs and renamed in 1769; gate, tiger-stone wall and 正觉寺 added by 1773, rebuilt in 1795. Jiaqing's growth came in three stages: the western and central groups of the Thirty Scenes first, then the new gate and eastern scenes, finally the south-west (招凉榭, 湛清轩, 畅和堂, 澄心堂, the shrines), gathered as a New Twenty Scenes.
- **E0722** (description, sure): 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 含辉楼. 2020 edition · v4 p.317 · S361. https://www.yuanmingyuanpark.cn/xs/yjbg/202008/P020200803382796786124.pdf#page=320
  Given to Prince Yongxuan about 1773 as 含晖园, to Princess Zhuangjing in 1801, returned in 1811 as 南园, when 联辉楼 was moved here from 西爽村. Main tower two storeys of seven bays, with a riding track 撤马道 south of it and 招凉榭, a five-bay open hall, on an islet. Its gates are 环翠 and the city-style south gate with Jiaqing's plaques 护松扉 and 排青幌. North of it lie 清夏斋 and 延英论道.

**On the plan:** Drawn on the plan of the gardens (S01), labelled 招凉榭, 12x4 cells. https://artmuseum.princeton.edu/collections/objects/138657
